name: Knuth–Morris–Pratt prefix-function matching
definition: For pattern p of length m≥1, π_i=max({0}∪{k:1≤k≤i and p[0:k]=p[i−k+1:i+1]}). Set π_0=0; for i=1,…,m−1 start q=π_{i−1}; while q>0 and p_q≠p_i set q←π_{q−1}; if p_q=p_i increment q; set π_i=q. For text t of length n≥0 start q=0; at each i=0,…,n−1 use the same fallback on p_q≠t_i, increment q on equality, and if q=m emit i−m+1 then reset q←π_{m−1}.
variables: p pattern; t text; m,n lengths; π_i longest proper border length of pattern prefix ending at i; q matched prefix length; i zero-based index; slices exclude right endpoint
assumptions: Finite pattern and text over a consistent equality relation, nonempty pattern, exact indices, no mutation during preprocessing or scanning; symbol comparisons and indexing have bounded constant cost
limitations: O(m+n) time and O(m) auxiliary storage excluding returned matches. Empty patterns are outside this specification; no approximate matching, wildcard or Unicode normalization semantics are implied
failure_conditions: Reject empty pattern, invalid equality semantics or stale prefix table
Do not access p_m after a match; reset to the longest proper border to preserve overlaps
computation: Build the prefix table with fallback to shorter previously computed borders; scan each text symbol once with the same fallback. Emit every zero-based start, including overlaps, and return an empty list for no matches.

source.citation: Knuth, Morris and Pratt (1977), Fast Pattern Matching in Strings, SIAM J. Comput. 6(2), 323–350, DOI 10.1137/0206024 (publisher abstract and metadata); Cornell CS 312 (2003), Lecture 27, KMP algorithm and prefix preprocessing. https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs312/2003sp/lectures/lec27.html

application: General exact sequence matching, including overlapping occurrences; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Nonempty finite pattern and finite text with declared symbol equality.
incompatible_methods: Treating exact equality as approximate similarity
Skipping overlap-producing fallback after a full match
mechanism_note: Every shorter viable alignment is a border of the already matched prefix; iterating proper borders enumerates these in decreasing length. The scan maintains the longest viable matched prefix, except that after emission it retains the longest proper border. Each fallback strictly decreases q and increases are at most one per processed symbol, giving linear total work. Cornell's prefix array is indexed by prefix length j, equivalent to π_{j−1}; the all-occurrences reset is independently derived. Distinct from suffix sorting and from Boyer–Moore majority cancellation, which is not string matching.

name: Suffix array prefix-doubling construction
definition: For sequence x of length n≥0, return [] if n=0. Otherwise set h=1 and assign dense nonnegative ranks r_i to symbols in ascending order; initialize SA by ascending r_i. While h<n and ranks are not unique, sort indices by K_i=(r_i,r_{i+h}) with r_{i+h}=−1 if i+h≥n. Assign dense new ranks starting at 0, equal exactly for equal pairs, indexed by original i; replace ranks simultaneously and set h←2h. Return SA in its final sorted order.
variables: x finite sequence; n length; i zero-based suffix start; h prefix span; r_i current dense rank; K_i ordered pair; SA permutation of nonempty suffix starts; −1 missing-block sentinel
assumptions: Static sequence with a consistent total order on symbols, lexicographic comparison with shorter proper prefixes first, exact integer ranks and safe index arithmetic; rank pairs read from the preceding round only
limitations: Comparison sorting gives O(n log²(n+1)) time and O(n) auxiliary space with a linear-space sort; bounded-integer stable radix sorting of dense ranks can reduce doubling rounds to O(n log(n+1)) total time including initial comparison sorting. No linear-time construction or accelerated query guarantee is implied
failure_conditions: Reject inconsistent symbol ordering and rank overflow or sentinel collisions
Do not update rank values during pair comparison; explicitly return the empty permutation for n=0
computation: Order and rank single symbols; repeatedly sort the suffix starts by pairs of old ranks with a missing-block sentinel, re-rank using a fresh array and double the span. Stop on unique ranks or full coverage; the sorted permutation is the result.

source.citation: Manber and Myers (1993), Suffix Arrays: A New Method for On-Line String Searches, SIAM J. Comput. 22(5), 935–948, DOI 10.1137/0222058 (bibliographic record and abstract); Kulcu, Advanced String Algorithms, §10.7.3 (pair-rank comparison-sort formulation). https://sercankulcu.github.io/files/algorithms/notes/Chapter_10_Advanced_String_Algorithms_Lecture_Notes.html

application: General static sequence indexing by lexicographically sorted suffixes; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Finite immutable sequence with declared total ordering of symbols.
incompatible_methods: Treating sorted cyclic rotations as nonempty suffixes
Mutating rank values while comparing keys
mechanism_note: Inductively ranks encode lexicographic order and equality of prefixes truncated at span h. Concatenating two adjacent truncated blocks gives the next prefix order; a missing second block ranks before any nonempty block. Distinct truncated prefixes fix their full suffix order, so early unique ranks are sufficient. When h≥n all distinct nonempty suffixes have been distinguished. Unlike KMP, this creates an index by repeated pair sorting rather than scanning a single fixed pattern. The comparison-sort specification is not a claim to implement the original paper's optimized sorting procedure.
